target.title: fix(runtime): guard JSON.stringify against circular tool output
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`writeRuntimeJson()` and the runtime `writeJson` method call `JSON.stringify(value)` on arbitrary tool return values. Circular references cause `TypeError: Converting circular structure to JSON`, crashing the output path.

Closes #99490 (improves on the contributor fix).

## Why This Change Was Made

Wrap both `JSON.stringify` call sites in `src/runtime.ts` with nested try-catch guards:

1. First try `JSON.stringify(value)` — normal path
2. Catch → try `JSON.stringify(String(value))` — handles ordinary circular refs (produces `"[object Object]"`)
3. Catch → output `"[unserializable]"` — last-resort for null-prototype circular objects where even `String()` throws

The contributor PR #99490 only had a single `String(value)` fallback, which ClawSweeper found can still throw for null-prototype circular objects (`Object.create(null)` with circular refs). This fix is fully non-throwing.

## User Impact

Prevents runtime crash when tools return objects with circular references. The CLI outputs a safe fallback string instead of crashing with `TypeError`.

## Evidence

### Unit tests (6/6 passed)
```
 ✓ writeRuntimeJson > serializes plain objects
 ✓ writeRuntimeJson > falls back to String(value) for circular references
 ✓ writeRuntimeJson > falls back to constant for null-prototype circular references
 ✓ writeRuntimeJson > delegates to runtime.log when writeStdout is absent
 ✓ writeRuntimeJson > falls back to String(value) in log path for circular references
 ✓ writeRuntimeJson > falls back to constant in log path for null-prototype circular references
```

### Live verification (all paths confirmed)
```
Test 1: Normal object → correct JSON output ✅
Test 2: Circular reference → "[object Object]" (no crash) ✅
Test 3: Null-prototype circular → "[unserializable]" (no crash) ✅
Test 4: writeRuntimeJson output path → handles circular ✅
Test 5: writeRuntimeJson log path → handles all 3 cases ✅
Test 6: defaultRuntime → handles all 3 cases ✅
```
